# Key numbers (generated by src/08_key_numbers.py; do not edit by hand)

## Act 1: job access in the Bay Area (Indeed + Opportunity Atlas)
- Indeed postings: 140,816 raw, 136,136 after removing duplicates (posted 2025-01-01 to 2026-09-21); 85% have parseable pay; 94% matched to a Census place.
- Bay Area postings: 45,312 (84% with pay). Bay Area tracts: 1,578 (1,568 with an Atlas outcome). Postings with licensed-profession titles (physician, dentist, NP...) not counted as entry-level: 3,357.
- Outcome: Opportunity Atlas mean adult household income rank of kids born 1978-83 to 25th-percentile families. Job data: 2025-2026. A comparison across eras, not a causal test.
- Median posted entry-level pay within R miles, by neighborhood mobility quintile (lowest -> highest):
  - 5 miles: $56,368, $55,120, $56,992, $57,814, $62,400
  - 10 miles: $57,200, $55,120, $58,240, $65,000, $67,500
  - 20 miles: $64,896, $64,490, $67,007, $67,810, $69,212
- Median number of entry-level postings (with pay) within 10 miles, same quintiles: 1,515, 1,053, 1,535, 1,828, 2,381 (1,564 tracts).
- Tracts with zero entry-level postings within 10 miles: 4.
- Does entry-level pay within R miles add to poverty + college share in predicting the Atlas outcome? (R2 change; coefficient per SD; p-value with standard errors clustered on ~10-mile grid cells)
  - 5 miles: R2 0.229 -> 0.233 (change +0.0038); coef +0.0044 rank points per SD; clustered p = 0.29; held-out-county R2 0.055 -> 0.069. Tracts weighted by number of children: change +0.0087, clustered p = 0.22
  - 10 miles: R2 0.231 -> 0.237 (change +0.0064); coef +0.0058 rank points per SD; clustered p = 0.31; held-out-county R2 0.059 -> 0.086. Tracts weighted by number of children: change +0.0206, clustered p = 0.11
  - 20 miles: R2 0.232 -> 0.247 (change +0.0155); coef +0.0086 rank points per SD; clustered p = 0.0095; held-out-county R2 0.062 -> 0.117. Tracts weighted by number of children: change +0.0300, clustered p = 0.00054
  - 10 miles, no-degree postings only: R2 0.231 -> 0.237 (change +0.0059); coef +0.0055 rank points per SD; clustered p = 0.36; held-out-county R2 0.059 -> 0.075. Tracts weighted by number of children: change +0.0191, clustered p = 0.15
  - Opportunity Insights' own measure: high-paying jobs within 5 miles, 2015: R2 0.232 -> 0.232 (change +0.0007); coef +0.0019 rank points per SD; clustered p = 0.44; held-out-county R2 0.062 -> 0.068. Tracts weighted by number of children: change +0.0102, clustered p = 0.032
- Spearman correlation with the Atlas outcome: entry pay within 5/10/20 mi 0.15 / 0.22 / 0.26; poverty share -0.45; college share 0.45.
- Bay Area entry-level postings that mention a bachelor's degree: 18%; they pay 19% more than postings that do not, in the same job family and city (95% CI 15-23%, clustered by employer); raw medians $104,510 vs $57,200; n = 17,892 postings.

## Data decisions (college)
- Colleges in the results file: 6,289. All-students earnings column: 3 distinct values across 5,831 colleges ($27,937, $36,041, $47,922) -> unusable.
- Target (median earnings of dependent students on federal aid, working and not enrolled, 10 years after entry, completers or not): 4,194 colleges, 3,350 distinct values.
- Reporting units (same dependent earnings, independent earnings and dependent debt): 3,489; 967 colleges (23%) share a unit with another campus (largest unit 23). Matching on earnings alone would have grouped 1,221.
- Matched to the lowest-income affordability row: 3,742 (89%); sector codes agree for 98.9%; HBCU flags agree for 100.0%.
- Minority-serving designations among the 4,194 colleges: HBCU 94, TCU 23, PBI 71, AANAPISI 184, HSI 536.

## Model (held-out test set)
- Split: 3,363 training / 831 test colleges (698 reporting units in test), whole units on one side. Grid search: 108 configurations, 5-fold grouped CV on training data. Best: {'learning_rate': 0.02, 'max_leaf_nodes': 31, 'min_samples_leaf': 20, 'l2_regularization': 0.0, 'max_iter': 1200}. Ridge baseline penalty chosen the same way: 3.16.
- National median: MAE $10,782 per college (95% CI $9,931-$11,623), $10,764 per reporting unit; median abs error 21.7%; R2 (log) -0.03
- Pell share + sector (linear): MAE $6,908 per college (95% CI $6,347-$7,506), $7,086 per reporting unit; median abs error 12.9%; R2 (log) 0.54
- All inputs (linear): MAE $4,981 per college (95% CI $4,566-$5,413), $5,006 per reporting unit; median abs error 9.1%; R2 (log) 0.72
- Our model (gradient-boosted trees): MAE $4,467 per college (95% CI $4,115-$4,852), $4,375 per reporting unit; median abs error 8.1%; R2 (log) 0.78
- Our model vs Pell + sector: MAE 35% lower; difference -$2,441 (95% CI -$2,886 to -$2,000). vs all-inputs linear: -$514 (95% CI -$817 to -$232).
- Cross-fitted predictions for all 4,194 colleges: MAE $4,364, R2 (log) 0.78; without race/ethnicity inputs MAE $4,575, R2 0.76.
- Most important inputs (permutation importance, test set): pell_share, sector, state, carnegie, pct_women.

## Opportunity colleges
- Rules: value-added >= +10%, Pell share >= 43% (median), net price for family income <= $30k at most $10,578 (median), 500+ students, own earnings figure.
- 75 of 2,408 ranked colleges qualify; median value-added +14%, median low-income net price $6,859. 61 still qualify without race/ethnicity inputs; 30 are within 3 points of the bar.
- By sector: Public 2-year 36, Public 4-year 29, Private nonprofit 4-year 7, Public <2-year 2, For-profit 4-year 1.
- Hispanic-serving institutions: 30 of 75 opportunity colleges (40%) vs 19% of all ranked colleges.
- California: 4 (West Hills College-Lemoore +18%; University of California-Merced +14%; California State University-Channel Islands +13%; Glendale Community College +12%).
- Bay Area: 0 of 41 ranked colleges qualify; 14 clear the value-added bar, 5 the Pell bar, 24 the price bar.
- Hidden gems (bottom 20% on raw earnings, value-added >= +10%): 24.
- Student parents at opportunity colleges with child-care data (70 of 75), center-based care: median gap $17,658; median total minimum-wage work needed about 50 hours/week (the source assumes 10 and adds the rest; the two medians are of different columns). Students without children: median gap $1,572, about 13 hours/week.

## Choosing a college (step 5b)
- Similar students: 555 colleges with Pell share >= 43% and expected earnings within 10% of $37,032. Median earnings by value-added quarter, lowest to highest: $33,211, $35,801, $37,497, $40,751 (gap $7,540); median low-income net price: $7,720, $7,824, $8,505, $8,755.
- Same comparison at 2,000+ students: gap $6,390, best quarter $2,638 dearer; at 5,000+: gap $5,561, best quarter $1,870 dearer. 4-year only: $8,069 (n=210); 2-year only: $6,118 (n=342).
- Rank correlation of low-income net price with raw earnings 0.38 and with value-added 0.09 (high-Pell colleges).
- Local choice sets (a high-Pell college plus same-level colleges within 25 miles at the same or lower price; 521 sets): the top raw earner is also the top value-added college in 48%.
- Top 20% by raw earnings (482 colleges): 13% have Pell share >= the median (vs 50% of ranked colleges); median low-income net price $14,762 vs $10,578.
- Also consider: 1,146 high-Pell starting colleges (63 tribal, specialized, online-by-design or closed ones are not compared). Stronger option within 25 miles: 45 colleges, 17,567 first-time Pell students a year. Comparable but none stronger: 177 colleges, 85,633. No comparable option: 924 colleges, 302,679; of these, no same-level college within 25 miles at all: 426 colleges, 110,041.
- Nearest stronger option: median earnings difference $6,239 a year, median price difference -$4,475, median 11.1 miles. 35 of 45 options are minority-serving; 8 HBCU/PBI starting colleges have an option, 4 of them pointed to a non-HBCU/PBI. All ranked colleges with a stronger option: 127.
- Independent-student test: independent students also earn more at the suggested college in 78% of 151 pairs (95% CI 70%-85%, resampling suggested colleges; pairs from 106 starting colleges of all Pell levels, 112 suggested colleges; median gap +13.4%), vs 47% of 479 pairs for the nearest comparable college. Across 15/25/50 miles and 5/10/15-point gaps: 71%-83%.
- Same starting colleges (55 with both a stronger option and another comparable college): independent students earn more at the nearest stronger option in 80% of cases vs 58% at the nearest other comparable college (difference 95% CI +9 to +36 points). Benchmark: across all comparable pairs, when dependent earnings are higher, independent earnings are also higher 71% of the time (430 pairs). Distinct suggested colleges: 36 (26 minority-serving).
- Coverage: ranked colleges enroll 73% of first-time, full-time Pell students (749,805 of 1,022,150).
